newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C. Bank says no devaluation discussions.
newsitem.headline: Manila C. Bank says no devaluation discussions.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor said on Wednesday there were no plans to discuss a peso devaluation at a Monetary Board meeting on Wednsday.
"The meeting today is a regular Monetary Board meeting. There is no item on the agenda on any discussion on the exchange rate," Gabriel Singson told Reuters.
"The exchange rate of the peso to the dollar shall not be administratively fixed but it will be left for determination by market forces in day-to-day transactions," Singson said.
"And the Central Bank will not hesitate to defend the currency against speculative attacks," he warned.

Singson gave his statements in reaction to a Singapore newspaper which quoted Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista as saying the devaluation of the peso will be taken up at today's Monetary Board meeting today.
The peso was hit by renewed speculation after the report was published, forcing the Central Bank to sell dollars heavily.
